description: We are “AgroSim,” a duo consisting of two students who love to code, science, and space. We have previously taken up projects based on coding, artificial intelligence, data, and research, and this time, we want to do something new using the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Both of us are quite curious people, who like to figure things out on the go.
summary:
AgroSim is a computational tool that helps farmers adapt to environmental changes, optimize planting systems and make smart decisions.
Our tool contains computational models that can simulate 88 different crops to explore plant growth, water usage, nutrient levels and soil fertility. Using NASA Earth observation and climate data, alongside soil and agricultural datasets, it integrates crop physiology and soil models to see how different strategies perform and to recommend the best ones to farmers.
In addition to crop planning, we have also included a dynamic ecosystem model which simulates interactions between microorganisms, weeds, pests, predators, and the soil environment. We also have a financial intelligence tool that uses USDA data to estimate production costs, potential income and economic trade-offs.
AgroSim addresses NASA's Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge by allowing farmers to compare different crops and planting strategies under changing environmental conditions and enabling them to implement highly efficient recommended rotations. This is important as farmers are under increasing pressure due to climate change, water scarcity, poor soil quality and economic challenges.
Overall, our tool aims to make sustainable farming more accessible by combining environmental factors, biology, economics and technology.
details:
1. What Does AgroSim Do?

A farmer needs to consider several factors when deciding what crop to grow. These factors include water availability, soil quality, environmental conditions and production costs.

We created AgroSim Global to bring these factors together. We have 88 crop models within our platform to give farmers insight into various crops, strategies and environments.

2. Crop Growth and Environmental Factors

We have crop models that simulate plant growth using NASA climate data. We considered factors such as:

  • Temperature, rainfall, sunlight and length of the growing season
  • Photosynthesis, root growth and biomass
  • Water availability, irrigation, drought and water usage
  • Nitrogen uptake, nutrients and soil fertility
  • Planting dates, maturity and harvest

We have models specific to certain crops and their growing needs, such as flooded rice, fruit trees and pineapple.

3. Soil Quality

We have a soil model that considers water, carbon, nitrogen, and organic matter across multiple growing seasons.

When a crop is harvested, remnants of the roots and plant matter are left in the soil. This provides nutrients and carbon to the soil, which can impact the next crop to be planted.

Farmers can see how certain crop rotations may affect soil quality in the long run.

4. Living Ecosystem

A unique aspect of AgroSim is having a living ecosystem model.

We have simulated interactions between weeds, herbivores, predators, microorganisms, detritivores and pathogens. Weeds compete with crops, predators influence herbivore populations and microorganisms help with nutrient recycling.

5. Financial

Not all crops will be profitable to grow.

We have a financial model that uses agricultural data from the USDA and regional cost benchmarks. This shows how much money could be made, how much would be spent, break even prices and economic trade offs.

We considered harvest times, crop prices, storage, marketable crops and the number of harvests per year. Farmers can compare not just environmental factors but financial factors as well.

6. User-Friendly

We wanted farmers to be able to understand their simulations. Our web application includes a map to select a location, images of crops and a 3D view of the farm with a timeline showing the growing season.

We have implemented multilingual voice recognition using Qwen 0.5B and Whisper tiny to make the platform more user friendly for farmers who speak different languages or prefer to speak.

7. Tools Used

We mainly used Python to create our simulation. We have mathematical models showing crop physiology, soil processes and ecosystem interactions.

We have used NASA environmental data, USDA agricultural data and OpenAI Codex for programming and debugging.

8. Creativity and Impact

What makes AgroSim different is that it combines crop growth, soil quality, living ecosystems and financial factors into one platform. We have considered climate change, water shortages, crop suitability, soil fertility, farming costs and user friendliness.

Our aim was to make agricultural modeling more accessible for farmers. This allows them to compare planting strategies, understand trade offs between environmental and financial factors and explore more sustainable ways to manage their farms.
